headline_en: Supreme Court will consider application to recall split verdict
headline_hi: सुप्रीम कोर्ट विभाजित फैसले को वापस लेने के आवेदन पर विचार करेगा

payload_en.headline: Supreme Court will consider application to recall split verdict

paragraphs.text: The Supreme Court of India said it would consider an application seeking the recall of its September 23 split verdict.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant stated that the Supreme Court will examine and take a call on the recall application.
A split verdict was pronounced on September 23 in a case challenging the Election Commissioners appointments law.

Due to a difference of opinion, the matter was ordered to be placed before CJI Kant on the administrative side for constitution of a bench of appropriate strength for an effective and authoritative adjudication.
A batch of pleas challenges the validity of the 2023 law governing the appointment of the CEC and ECs.
An earlier Constitution Bench judgment in the Anoop Baranwal case had included the Chief Justice of India as a neutral member in the Prime Minister-led selection panel for CECs and ECs.

Sections 7 and 8 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023 establish a selection panel consisting of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and a Union Cabinet Minister.

The Centre sought the matter's reference to a larger bench, arguing that it raised a constitutional question, with Justice Dipankar Datta declining the request and Justice Satish Chandra Sharma supporting it.

Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan stated that the recall application had earlier been mentioned before a bench headed by Justice Datta, but the matter was subsequently released from that bench and he was asked to mention it before the CJI.
A curative petition has also been filed in addition to the recall application.
The 2023 law excludes the Chief Justice of India from the panel for selecting the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners.
An interlocutory application is a formal request filed during an ongoing case seeking a specific interim order or direction.
A split verdict occurs when an even-numbered bench of judges cannot reach a unanimous decision or a majority consensus because they hold opposing views on a case.
In the case of a split verdict, the case is referred to a larger bench where the Chief Justice places it before an odd-numbered bench for a rehearing.

On September 23, a two-judge Supreme Court bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma delivered a split opinion on whether petitions contesting the 2023 law governing the appointment of the CEC and ECs should be referred to a larger Constitution bench.
A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma gave split opinions on whether a batch of pleas challenging the validity of a 2023 law should be referred to a larger Constitution bench.

A two-judge bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma delivered divergent opinions on the Centre's plea seeking reference of petitions challenging the 2023 law to a larger Constitution Bench.
Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma delivered separate opinions on the issue of whether challenges to the 2023 law should be referred to a larger Constitution Bench.
The Supreme Court delivered a split verdict on September 23 regarding whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the CEC and ECs should be heard by a five-judge Bench.
Justice Dipankar Datta held that a two-judge Bench could hear the challenge.
Justice Dipankar Datta declined the Centre's request to refer the challenge to a larger Constitution bench, while Justice Satish Chandra Sharma favoured placing the matter before a larger panel.

Justice Dipankar Datta declined the Centre's request for reference of the challenge to a larger Constitution Bench, while Justice Satish Chandra Sharma favoured placing the matter before a larger bench.
Justice Dipankar Datta held that reference of petitions challenging the 2023 law to a larger bench was not necessary, while Justice Satish Chandra Sharma favoured a larger bench.
Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Satish Chandra Sharma delivered separate opinions on September 23 on petitions challenging Sections 7 and 8 of the 2023 Act.
Both judges on the Bench passed a common order for the Chief Justice of India to allocate the case to a Constitution Bench.
Senior advocate Sankaranarayanan mentioned a recall application before a Supreme Court bench comprising Chief Justice of India Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana in New Delhi.

The Supreme Court agreed to examine a plea seeking the recall of its recent split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners should be referred to a larger Constitution bench.
Senior advocate Sankaranarayanan told the Supreme Court bench about the recall application.

Sankaranarayanan mentioned an application before the Supreme Court seeking a recall of its recent split verdict on petitions challenging the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023.

Chief Justice of India Kant agreed to examine and take a call on hearing an application seeking a recall of a split verdict pronounced on September 23 in the Election Commissioners appointments law case.
Senior advocate Sankaranarayanan informed a bench led by Chief Justice of India Kant about a recall application regarding the September 23 split verdict.
Senior advocate Sankaranarayanan mentioned the plea before Chief Justice of India Kant.

Sankaranarayanan stated that he had previously mentioned the application before a bench headed by Justice Dipankar Datta, who asked him to mention the matter before the current bench after releasing it from his board.
Naman Sherstra filed the application, which was previously mentioned before Justice Dipankar Datta.
Justice Dipankar Datta asked senior advocate Sankaranarayanan to mention the application before the Chief Justice as the records had been returned to the CJI.
The application objected to the common order without specifically challenging the separate opinion given by Justice Dipankar Datta.
The 2023 law replaced the CJI with a Union Minister nominated by the Prime Minister in the selection panel.
Sherstra did not impute actual bias, motive, or want of good faith on the part of Justice Satish Chandra Sharma.
Siddharth Sharma was appointed as the standing counsel for the ECI before the Madhya Pradesh High Court on July 10, 2024.
Senior advocate Sankaranarayanan stated that a curative petition had also been filed alongside the independent recall application.

A LiveLaw report stated that the application seeking recall of the judgment has been filed citing a reasonable apprehension of bias involving Justice Satish Chandra Sharma, whose son is a standing counsel for the Election Commission of India.
Another party has filed a curative petition against the split verdict, Sankaranarayanan said.
Dr Jaya Thakur filed a separate curative petition contending that Justice Satish Chandra Sharma should not have heard the matter due to an alleged direct conflict of interest.

Dr Jaya Thakur argued that there was a reasonable apprehension of bias and propriety because Justice Satish Chandra Sharma's son, Siddharth Sharma, has been serving as standing counsel for the Election Commission of India before the Madhya Pradesh High Court since July 2024.

Sherstra stated that the application questions why Justice Satish Chandra Sharma did not reveal during multiple court proceedings that his son was a standing counsel for the Election Commission of India.
Sherstra sought a recall of the opinion given by Justice Satish Chandra Sharma on September 23 on the question of referring the challenge to a five-judge Bench.
Justice Dipankar Datta observed that the 2023 law was prima facie wrong to ignore an earlier Constitution Bench judgment in the Anoop Baranwal case.
Justice Dipankar Datta stated that the replacement gave the Executive veto power over appointments and reduced the Opposition Leader's presence to an ornamental status.
Media reports alleged that Justice Satish Chandra Sharma’s son was a standing counsel for the Election Commission of India subsequent to the September 23 verdict.
Petitioner Jaya Thakur filed a curative petition on September 29 to recall the split verdict, alleging reasonable apprehension of bias and propriety.
Sherstra stated that Justice Satish Chandra Sharma did not disclose the engagement of his son to the parties during the five hearings in the matter on May 5, May 7, May 14, May 27 and July 30.

Senior advocate Sankaranarayanan stated that the recall application was earlier mentioned before a bench headed by Justice Datta, released from that bench, and subsequently presented before the Chief Justice of India.
Justice Satish Chandra Sharma’s son was working as a lawyer for the Election Commission of India during the hearings, Petitioners said.
The non-disclosure of Justice Satish Chandra Sharma’s son's role created a suspicion of bias, Petitioners said.
Justice Satish Chandra Sharma favoured a five-judge Bench.
A related petition challenged the appointments of Gyanesh Kumar, who is now the Chief Election Commissioner, and Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu.
Rahul Gandhi-led opposition demanded CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over the poll body's special intensive revision exercise.
Following the split verdict, the matter was placed before the Chief Justice of India on the administrative side for constitution of a bench of appropriate strength.

आवेदन ने न्यायमूर्ति दीपांकर दत्ता द्वारा दी गई अलग राय को विशेष रूप से चुनौती दिए बिना सामान्य आदेश पर आपत्ति जताई।
2023 के कानून ने चयन पैनल में प्रधान मंत्री द्वारा नामित एक केंद्रीय मंत्री के साथ सीजेआई को बदल दिया।
Sherstra ने न्यायमूर्ति Satish Chandra Sharma की ओर से किसी वास्तविक पूर्वग्रह, मंशा या सदभावना की कमी का आरोप नहीं लगाया।
सिद्धार्थ शर्मा को 10 जुलाई, 2024 को मध्य प्रदेश उच्च न्यायालय के समक्ष ईसीआई के लिए स्थायी वकील के रूप में नियुक्त किया गया था।
वरिष्ठ अधिवक्ता Sankaranarayanan ने कहा कि स्वतंत्र रिकॉल आवेदन के साथ एक क्यूरेटिव याचिका भी दायर की गई है।

LiveLaw की एक रिपोर्ट में कहा गया है कि फैसले को वापस लेने की मांग करने वाला आवेदन न्यायमूर्ति Satish Chandra Sharma से जुड़े पूर्वग्रह की एक उचित आशंका का हवाला देते हुए दायर किया गया है, जिनके बेटे भारत के चुनाव आयोग के लिए स्टैंडिंग काउंसिल हैं।
Sankaranarayanan ने कहा कि एक अन्य पक्ष ने विभाजित फैसले के खिलाफ क्यूरेटिव याचिका दायर की है।
डॉ. जया ठाकुर ने एक अलग सुधारात्मक याचिका यह तर्क देते हुए दायर की कि कथित प्रत्यक्ष हित के टकराव के कारण न्यायमूर्ति को मामले की सुनवाई नहीं करनी चाहिए थी।

डॉ. जया ठाकुर ने तर्क दिया कि पूर्वाग्रह और औचित्य की उचित आशंका थी क्योंकि न्यायमूर्ति सतीश चंद्र शर्मा के बेटे, सिद्धार्थ शर्मा, जुलाई 2024 से मध्य प्रदेश उच्च न्यायालय के समक्ष भारत के चुनाव आयोग के लिए स्थायी वकील के रूप में सेवा दे रहे हैं।
Sherstra ने कहा कि आवेदन यह सवाल उठाता है कि न्यायमूर्ति Satish Chandra Sharma ने कई अदालती कार्यवाही के दौरान यह क्यों नहीं बताया कि उनके बेटे भारत के चुनाव आयोग के लिए स्टैंडिंग काउंसिल हैं।
Sherstra ने पांच-न्यायाधीशों की बेंच को चुनौती भेजने के सवाल पर 23 सितंबर को न्यायमूर्ति Satish Chandra Sharma द्वारा दी गई राय को वापस लेने की मांग की।
न्यायमूर्ति दीपांकर दत्ता ने देखा कि अनूप बरनवाल मामले में पहले के संविधान पीठ के फैसले को नजरअंदाज करना प्रथम दृष्टया गलत था।
न्यायमूर्ति दीपांकर दत्ता ने कहा कि प्रतिस्थापन ने कार्यपालिका को नियुक्तियों पर वीटो शक्ति दी और विपक्ष के नेता की उपस्थिति को एक अलंकृत स्थिति तक कम कर दिया।
मीडिया रिपोर्टों में आरोप लगाया गया कि न्यायमूर्ति सतीश चंद्र शर्मा के बेटे 23 सितंबर के फैसले के बाद भारत के चुनाव आयोग के लिए स्थायी वकील थे।
याचिकाकर्ता जया ठाकुर ने पूर्वाग्रह और औचित्य की उचित आशंका का आरोप लगाते हुए विभाजित फैसले को वापस लेने के लिए 29 सितंबर को एक सुधारात्मक याचिका दायर की।
Sherstra ने कहा कि न्यायमूर्ति Satish Chandra Sharma ने इस मामले की पांच सुनवाइयों 5 मई, 7 मई, 14 मई, 27 मई और 30 जुलाई के दौरान पक्षों के सामने अपने बेटे की नियुक्ति का खुलासा नहीं किया।

वरिष्ठ अधिवक्ता Sankaranarayanan ने कहा कि रिकॉल आवेदन का जिक्र पहले न्यायमूर्ति Datta की अध्यक्षता वाली बेंच के समक्ष किया गया था, उस बेंच से मुक्त किया गया, और बाद में भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश के समक्ष प्रस्तुत किया गया।
याचिकाकर्ताओं ने कहा कि सुनवाइयों के दौरान न्यायमूर्ति Satish Chandra Sharma के बेटे भारत के चुनाव आयोग के लिए एक वकील के रूप में काम कर रहे थे।
याचिकाकर्ताओं ने कहा कि न्यायमूर्ति Satish Chandra Sharma के बेटे की भूमिका का खुलासा न करने से पूर्वग्रह का संदेह पैदा हुआ।
Justice Satish Chandra Sharma favoured a five-judge Bench.
A related petition challenged the appointments of Gyanesh Kumar, who is now the Chief Election Commissioner, and Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu.
Rahul Gandhi-led opposition demanded CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over the poll body's special intensive revision exercise.
Following the split verdict, the matter was placed before the Chief Justice of India on the administrative side for constitution of a bench of appropriate strength.

वरिष्ठ अधिवक्ता गोपाल शंकरनारायणन ने सुप्रीम कोर्ट की पीठ को पुनर्विचार आवेदन के बारे में बताया।
